findings.detail: the package cannot be imported, so neither execution branch and therefore no collective is ever reached. model/model.py:11 does "from .layers import MLP, RQLayer" but model/layers.py does not exist in the tree; model/curvature_control.py:19 does "from model.frechet_poincare import clamp_ball, poincare_distance" but model/frechet_poincare.py does not exist; there is also no model/__init__.py, so train_rqvae.py:37 "from model import RQVAE" fails as well. The failure is at import time, i.e. before dist.init_process_group (train_rqvae.py:328) and before the four-rank launch in _launch_via_torchrun (train_rqvae.py:646-674), so the codebook broadcast at :435, the two loss all_reduces at :543-544 and the barriers at :436/:591/:640 are unreachable code. The diff quoted in the brief (model/layers.py:207-213 commitment detach, and the new tests/test_curvature_switch_apply.py) was never applied to this tree: both files are absent, so the previous blocking finding about the un-detached commitment on the code side is neither fixed nor verifiable here.

findings.reproduction: from the tree root, "ls model" shows only model.py and curvature_control.py; "python -c 'import model.model'" raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'model.layers'; "python -c 'import model.curvature_control'" raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'model.frechet_poincare'; "torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 train_rqvae.py" therefore dies on all four ranks at the first import, exactly as the GENREC_SINGLE_GPU=1 single-card branch does (train_rqvae.py:648-652 only skips the fork, it does not fix the imports).

findings.correction: ship the layer that reads it — assignment_cost and the curved commitment must call squared_distance_c(x, code, self.curvature()) — and add a test that changing frechet.curvature on a fixed latent changes the argmin codes.
findings.detail: the per-level curvature the whole mechanism is built on is written to layer.frechet.curvature, and nothing in this tree ever reads it back. The only reader named by the brief's own diff is VQLayer.curvature() in model/layers.py, which is absent, so the switch-driven scalar produced by level_curvatures (curvature_control.py:136-142) terminates in a plain Python attribute of the frechet helper. Because layers.py is gone, a missing frechet attribute would not even raise: line 493 would silently create it. The applied value is therefore not shown to reach the distance, the assignment or the commitment, and the DDP symmetry question (all ranks must run the same metric) cannot be answered for a value no rank consumes. This is the same structural hole the previous review reported, now relocated: the switch code exists (level_curvatures is called), but the applied channel still dead-ends outside the shipped tree.
findings.location: train_rqvae.py:490-493 (the only writer of the applied curvature)
findings.reproduction: "grep -rn curvature" over the four shipped files yields the writers curvature_control.py:106/116/130 (exp0_c / log0_c / squared_distance_c parameters) and train_rqvae.py:493, and no site that reads layer.frechet.curvature back into a distance: model/layers.py, the file that must contain it, does not exist.

findings.check: shared state: codebook, cache and counters across ranks
findings.correction: broadcast the parameter itself (dist.broadcast(layer.embed.weight.data, 0), or expose a codebook_parameter() that returns the leaf tensor) and do the same inside apply_frechet_codebook_step; additionally run init_codebook on rank 0 only (guard :426 with rank == 0) or decouple the model seed from the rank (set_seed(SEED) for the model, SEED + rank only for the sampler), so the broadcast corrects rounding rather than being the only thing keeping four different codebooks together.
findings.detail: the only synchronisation of the codebook initialisation is dist.broadcast(layer.get_code_embs().data, 0), and get_code_embs() is not guaranteed to be the parameter. The trainer builds the layer with tangent_codebook=True, and the comment at :272-274 states the table is "a tangent-space table, mapped at the measured curvature by every step"; model/model.py:80 also writes through the same accessor, layer.get_code_embs().data.copy_(moved). If get_code_embs() is the documented derived view exp0_c(weight, curvature) rather than the parameter, both writes target a temporary: the collective still executes (so no hang and the test's all_reduce stays matched), but rank 0's KMeans start is discarded and the four ranks keep the different KMeans results each computed at :426 under the per-rank seed from :338. Every later step then runs four different codebooks, the assignment differs per rank, and the exported SID is whatever rank 0 happened to hold. The defect is currently unverifiable because get_code_embs has no definition anywhere in the tree — which is itself the problem: the only test that would pin it (tests/test_ddp.py:56-57 and :99-103) reads the same accessor and is unrunnable (it imports model.model and is skipped outside torchrun). Note also that broadcast_buffers=False means DDP never re-syncs buffers, so nothing else corrects a lost initialisation.
findings.reproduction: grep for get_code_embs in the shipped tree returns only call sites (model/model.py:61,79,80; train_rqvae.py:435,481,492; tests/test_ddp.py:57,100,103) and never a definition, so no shipped code shows the broadcast target is a leaf nn.Parameter. After shipping layers.py the check is: is layer.get_code_embs().data_ptr() == layer.embed.weight.data_ptr()? If not, line 435 broadcasts into a temporary and the initialisation is unsynchronised.
